scope: Eleventh expansion batch: 12 exercises, three hou comparisons, three hoka additions, and three each for affirmative and negative advice with hou ga ii. Hoka exclusion/no-other-option uses are not separate targets in this batch.

sources.section: Using hou for comparisons and using yori: hou reading of 方, noun + no, and comparison against another alternative. The simplified extraction loses some Japanese inline text; the explanatory prose itself supplies noun attachment and comparative scope. No claim is based on a missing example string.

Inspected actual HTML Structure and About sections, not the forum excerpt returned by simplified extraction: verb ta-form + 方 + が + いい for advice; dictionary-form variants exist; the phrase can be direct. The blanket politeness recommendation for ba ii is not adopted. The Related section also explains X yori Y no hou ga as a comparison favoring Y on the stated property.
Negative advice: verb nai-form + 方 + が + いい suggests it is better not to do the action; it can be direct rather than automatically gentle.

Inspected entry 他, reading ほか, spellings 他 and 外: sense 5 for addition, with noun + no hoka (ni) and verb + hoka (ni); sense 4 distinguishes exclusion in negative sentences. Dictionary inclusion of both spellings is not a claim of equal frequency.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are newly authored. Sources support patterns and spellings, not automatic attestation of each new collocation or correctness of every distractor rationale.

Six noun-choice items visibly limit the list to hou and hoka, with kana/kanji accepted. Each noun has two noun + no frames and one directly attached verb-clause frame. The comparative examples supply concrete weights, temperatures or journey times rather than infer a preference from an unstated stereotype.

Six advice items visibly request only the supplied verb's ta or nai form before printed hou ga ii. The same three verbs occur in both advice directions. Kana/kanji spellings are explicit; yonda illustrates that ta-form includes da endings, and tomorrow's itta does not report a past trip.

Screen the full article inventory: ue can also add a fact; beki, koto da and other expressions can convey advice. These are outside the visible literal-blank tasks, not universally invalid. Dictionary-form affirmative hou ga ii is also possible outside the stated form restriction.

One canonical SRS identity per exercise, not per spelling or presentation. These tasks cover comparison, addition and advice realization, not every hou/hoka sense or unrestricted choice between all advice expressions.
All prior 143 exercise records remain unchanged.
